mainTopic: Witnesses as judges for קידוש החודש, why a cow's horn is not a kosher שופר, and rare words learned from other lands
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא rules that a witness to a murder cannot also judge the case. The גמרא limits this to דיני נפשות, where the court must search for reasons to acquit, so for קידוש החודש even רבי עקיבא agrees a witness may judge. A new משנה then rules that every שופר is kosher except a cow's horn, because it is called a קרן, and רבי יוסי objects that every שופר is called a קרן. The גמרא explains the רבנן: other horns are called both שופר and קרן, but a cow's horn is called only קרן. רבי יוסי answers with the verse 'שור פר', which he reads as 'שופר'. עולא gives another reason: a cow recalls the עגל הזהב, and אין קטיגור נעשה סניגור. The גמרא tests this rule against the פר's blood, the gold vessels, and the בגדי זהב. אביי gives a third reason: a layered cow's horn looks like several שופרות. רבי יוסי answers each of these reasons. Finally, רבי עקיבא's report from ערביא proves that יובל means a ram, which leads to a list of rare biblical words explained from how people spoke in other places, and a story about לוי that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא on Whether Witnesses Can Become Judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא. רבי טרפון says some of the judges who saw a murder serve as witnesses and others serve as judges. רבי עקיבא says they all become witnesses, because a witness cannot be a judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some of them become witnesses and some become judges. These are the words of רבי טרפון. רבי עקיבא says: they all become witnesses, and a witness cannot become a judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא. It is using this source to suggest that our משנה, which lets witnesses to the new moon also be judges, does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, judges of the סנהדרין saw a person commit murder. רבי טרפון lets the group split into two roles, with some testifying and the rest judging. רבי עקיבא forbids this completely, so the ברייתא appears to contradict our משנה if the משנה is to follow רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness cannot become a judge

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of the ברייתא. The case is about judges who themselves saw a murder, not about the new moon. The גמרא brings it up only to compare it with our משנה about קידוש החודש.

phrases.english: some of them become witnesses
and some of them become judges,
these are the words of Rabbi Tarfon.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּן נַעֲשִׂין עֵדִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: all of them become witnesses,
and a witness cannot become a judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְצָתָן נַעֲשׂוּ עֵדִים וּמִקְצָתָן נַעֲשׂוּ דַּיָּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source the גמרא began quoting on the previous amud, to show that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה, which allows witnesses to become judges, does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא rules that a witness cannot become a judge.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's Rule Applies Only to Capital Cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי עקיבא's rule applies only in דיני נפשות, where the court must search for reasons to acquit. For the new moon, even רבי עקיבא agrees that a witness can be a judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say our משנה follows רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא said his rule there only for capital cases. The Torah says 'the congregation shall judge' and 'the congregation shall save,' so the court must try to save the accused. Once the judges saw him kill a person, they cannot find any merit for him. But here, even רבי עקיבא agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the proof from the ברייתא. It shows that our משנה can follow רבי עקיבא after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah requires the court in a murder case to actively look for ways to save the defendant, as it says 'והצילו העדה'. A judge who personally watched the murder can no longer look at the defendant favorably, so he cannot fulfill that duty. Sighting the new moon involves no such duty to acquit, so the reason behind רבי עקיבא's rule does not apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. This introduces a defense showing the opinion still fits.
He only said his rule up to this point. This limits a ruling to its original case.
Capital cases, where a life is at stake
And the congregation shall save. The verse that obligates the court to seek acquittal.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's rule that 'a witness cannot be a judge' is based on the duty to search for acquittal in capital cases. For קידוש החודש, even רבי עקיבא agrees that a witness may judge.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method in the גמרא. Once you find the reason behind a תנא's rule, you can limit that rule to the cases where the reason applies.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva only said his view
there, regarding capital cases,
for the Merciful One said: "And the congregation shall judge"
"and the congregation shall save,"
and once they saw him kill a person,
they are unable to see merit for him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא — אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מוֹדֶה.
phrases.english: But here, even Rabbi Akiva agrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא by limiting רבי עקיבא's rule to capital cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that our משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רבי עקיבא's rule applies everywhere. In fact it comes from the duty to seek acquittal, which exists only in דיני נפשות.

steps.title: New משנה: Every שופר Is Kosher Except a Cow's Horn
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that all שופרות are kosher, except one made from a cow's horn, because that is called a קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All שופרות are kosher, except for that of a cow, because it is a 'קרן' (horn).
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins with a new משנה about which animal horns may be used as a שופר. The first opinion, the תנא קמא, excludes a cow's horn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא's reasoning depends on names. The מצוה requires a 'שופר', and a cow's horn is called a 'קרן' instead, so it does not qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: שופרות, animal horns used for blowing
Horn. Here it means a name different from 'שופר'.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: All shofars are kosher,
except for that of a cow,
because it is a 'keren' (horn).

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת כְּשֵׁרִים חוּץ מִשֶּׁל פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the previous discussion about witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every animal horn is kosher for שופר except a cow's horn, because it is called 'קרן' and not 'שופר'.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: Every שופר Is Called a קרן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי challenges the תנא קמא's reasoning. He cites a verse in which a ram's horn, the classic שופר, is also called a 'קרן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: But aren't all שופרות called 'קרן'? As it says: 'When they sound a long blast with the קרן of the ram.'
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the משנה, רבי יוסי argues that the תנא קמא's reason does not work. If being called 'קרן' disqualified a horn, then a ram's horn would be disqualified too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in יהושע calls a ram's horn a 'קרן היובל', and a ram's horn is certainly a kosher שופר. So the name 'קרן' cannot be a reason to disqualify, and רבי יוסי concludes that a cow's horn should be kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so? This introduces a challenge.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא כׇּל הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת נִקְרְאוּ קֶרֶן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: But aren't all shofars called 'keren',
as it says: "When they sound a long blast with the horn of the ram."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of the תנא קמא in the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's reason that a cow's horn is disqualified because it is called 'קרן'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A kosher ram's horn is also called 'קרן', so that name cannot be what disqualifies a horn.

steps.title: רבי יוסי Makes Sense, So What Do the רבנן Say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוסי's argument sounds convincing. It then asks how the רבנן can disagree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יוסי is speaking well. And the רבנן, how do they answer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move. It admits רבי יוסי's point is strong and asks what the רבנן would answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'שפיר קאמר' means the argument looks hard to refute. The real question is what the רבנן's view could rest on.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying well, a convincing argument
The Rabbis, here the תנא קמא

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Yosei is speaking well!
And the Rabbis? (How do they respond?)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יוסי's challenge by asking for the רבנן's reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן can hold their position given רבי יוסי's convincing proof.

steps.title: Other Horns Are Also Called שופר, but a Cow's Is Not
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain that other horns are called both שופר and קרן. A cow's horn is called only קרן and never שופר, as shown from the verse about the firstborn ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: All other שופרות are called 'שופר' and are also called 'קרן.' But a cow's horn is called 'קרן' and is never called 'שופר,' as it is written: 'His firstborn ox, grandeur is his, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's answer to רבי יוסי. The problem with a cow's horn is not that it is called 'קרן'. The problem is that it is never called 'שופר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי showed that kosher horns can be called 'קרן', and the רבנן agree with that. Their point is that kosher horns also carry the name 'שופר', while the Torah refers to an ox's horns only as 'קרנים'. Since the מצוה requires a 'שופר', a horn that never has that name does not qualify.
steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, being called 'קרן' is not the problem. The problem is lacking the name 'שופר'. A cow's horn is called only 'קרן', so it is not kosher for the מצוה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the רבנן disagree with רבי יוסי's verse. They accept that a ram's horn is called 'קרן'. They add that it is also called 'שופר', which a cow's horn never is.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת אִקְּרוֹ שׁוֹפָר וְאִקְּרוֹ קֶרֶן.
phrases.english: All shofars are called 'shofar' and are called 'keren.'
That of a cow is called 'keren,'
but it is not called 'shofar,'
as it is written: "His firstborn ox, grandeur is his,
and his horns are the horns of a wild ox."

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַשּׁוֹפָרוֹת אִקְּרוֹ שׁוֹפָר וְאִקְּרוֹ קֶרֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by explaining the רבנן's position.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Other horns have both names, 'שופר' and 'קרן'. A cow's horn has only the name 'קרן', as the verse about the ox shows, so it lacks the required name 'שופר'.

steps.title: רבי יוסי shows a cow is also called שופר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rejects the רבנן's claim that a cow's horn is never called שופר. He reads 'שור פר' in תהלים as one word: 'משופר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי would answer you: a cow is also called שופר. The verse says 'And it shall please ה׳ better than an ox-bull (שור פר).' If it is a שור, why call it a פר? And if it is a פר, why call it a שור? So what does 'שור פר' mean? It means 'than a שופר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוסי defends himself against the רבנן's proof from step 6. He brings a verse where a cow's horn is called a שופר after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said a cow is only called קרן, never שופר. רבי יוסי notices that 'שור פר' is a doubled, strange phrase. He reads the two words together as 'משופר'. If that reading is right, a cow is called שופר too, and the רבנן's distinction falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you. This formula introduces how a sage would answer a challenge.
Ox-bull. This is the unusual double phrase in תהלים סט:לב.
Than a שופר. This is רבי יוסי's reading of the two words joined together.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not changing the letters of the verse. He is only reading the two words 'שור פר' as if they were joined into one word, 'שופר'.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei would say to you:
that a cow is also called a shofar,
as it is written: 'And it shall please the Lord better than an ox-bull,'
if it is an ox (shor), why say bull (par)?
And if it is a bull (par), why say ox (shor)?
Rather, what is 'shor par'? It means 'than a shofar.'
phrases.notes: The two words are read as one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבנן's proof in step 6, which said a cow is only called קרן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the רבנן's claim that a cow is never called שופר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רבנן overlooked a verse where a cow's horn can be read as 'שופר'.

steps.title: The רבנן read 'שור פר' as an ox as big as a bull
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain the doubled phrase in a different way, following רב מתנה: an ox that has grown as large as a פר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They hold like רב מתנה. רב מתנה said: what does 'שור פר' mean? An ox that is as big as a פר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the רבנן deal with רבי יוסי's verse. It answers that they explain the double phrase another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's proof depended on the phrase 'שור פר' being impossible to read as two separate words. רב מתנה gives a plain meaning: a שור that has reached the size of a פר. Once the phrase makes sense as written, there is no need to read it as 'משופר', and the רבנן's position stands.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose explanation the רבנן follow here
And the רבנן? This asks how the other side answers the argument.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? They explain as Rav Mattana did.
For Rav Mattana said:
What is 'shor par'? An ox that is as large as a bull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the רבנן against רבי יוסי's reading in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שור פר' makes no sense as two words, so it must mean 'משופר'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שור פר' means an ox grown as large as a פר, so the verse does not call a cow's horn a שופר.

steps.title: עולא's reason: a prosecutor cannot become a defender
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives a different reason for the רבנן, based on רב חסדא. The כהן גדול does not wear gold in the קודש הקדשים, because gold recalls the עגל הזהב. A cow's horn would recall the calf in the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: this is the reason of the רבנן, following רב חסדא. רב חסדא said: why does the כהן גדול not enter the inner sanctum in בגדי זהב to do the service? Because a prosecutor cannot become a defender.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא offers a brand-new reason why the רבנן disqualify a cow's horn. This reason is not about the verse's wording at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור, the כהן גדול goes into the קודש הקדשים in white linen, not gold. Gold would remind Heaven of the עגל הזהב, our 'prosecutor', and the service there is meant to plead for us as a 'defender'. The שופר of ראש השנה also works as a plea for us. So a cow's horn, which recalls the calf, cannot be used.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who offers an alternative reason
The gold garments of the כהן גדול
The innermost place, the קודש הקדשים

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'אין קטיגור נעשה סניגור' is a famous principle. It explains several laws about what may be used when asking for forgiveness.
steps.confusionAlert: The word זהב here points to the עגל הזהב, the Golden Calf. That is why a cow's horn is linked to the gold garments: both bring the same sin to mind.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
This is the reason of the Rabbis, in line with Rav Ḥisda.
For Rav Ḥisda said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֵין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל נִכְנָס
phrases.english: For what reason does the High Priest not enter
in golden garments into the innermost sanctum
to perform the service?
Because a prosecutor cannot become a defender.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the verse-based reason with a reason based on the logic of 'prosecutor and defender'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cow's horn is not kosher because it recalls the עגל הזהב, and a prosecutor cannot become a defender.

steps.title: But the blood of a bull is brought inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's rule. On יום כיפור, the blood of a פר is brought into the קודש הקדשים, even though a bovine recalls the calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it not so? But there is the blood of the פר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the principle עולא just used. It points to a case that seems to break the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If anything from cattle reminds us of the עגל הזהב, the פר of יום כיפור should be a problem too. Yet its blood is sprinkled right in the קודש הקדשים. This seems to contradict 'אין קטיגור נעשה סניגור'.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is... This phrase introduces a counter-example.
The blood of the bull sprinkled on יום כיפור

phrases.english: And is it not so? But there is the blood of the bull!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle that עולא brought in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that a prosecutor cannot become a defender
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood of a פר, which recalls the calf, is brought into the קודש הקדשים. So something linked to the sin is used there after all.

steps.title: The blood has changed, so it does not recall the sin
steps.stepSummary: Blood is not the animal itself. Since it has changed form, it does not bring the עגל הזהב to mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it has changed, it has changed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Blood does not count, because it no longer looks like a cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule only applies to something that visibly recalls the sin, like gold or a cow's horn. Blood has been transformed and does not look like the animal, so it does not act as a 'prosecutor'. The rule stays in place, and so does עולא's reason for the רבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for the רבנן that a cow's horn is not kosher. (1) The verse: a cow is only called קרן, and 'שור פר' means an ox as big as a פר. (2) עולא: a cow's horn recalls the עגל הזהב, and a prosecutor cannot become a defender. Blood does not count, because it has changed form.

phrases.english: Since it has changed, it has changed.
phrases.notes: It is only blood, not the animal, so it does not recall the sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from the blood of the פר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything from cattle should be forbidden in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only something that visibly recalls the calf is a problem. Blood has changed form, so it is allowed.

steps.title: But the Ark, its cover and the cherubs are gold and sit inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's rule. The ארון, the כפורת and the כרובים are all made of gold, yet they are inside the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the Ark, the Ark cover and the cherub, which are gold and are in the Holy of Holies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule that gold cannot be in the קודש הקדשים. It points to gold objects that are always there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said gold reminds ה׳ of the עגל הזהב, so it should not be in the קודש הקדשים. But the most central items in that room, the ארון, the כפורת and the כרובים, are covered in gold. So the rule as stated seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is… (opens a challenge from a known fact)
The gold cover on top of the Ark
Cherub, the gold figures on the Ark cover

phrases.english: But there is the Ark, the Ark cover, and the cherub!
phrases.notes: All of these are gold and sit permanently inside the Holy of Holies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the blood question was answered, the גמרא raises a new challenge to רב חסדא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that gold may not be used in the קודש הקדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gold objects are permanently in the קודש הקדשים, so gold there cannot be forbidden across the board.

steps.title: The rule is only about a sinner bringing gold in
steps.stepSummary: The rule is not that no gold may be in the room. It is that a sinner seeking atonement should not bring gold in with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What we are saying is that a sinner should not bring in gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רב חסדא's rule. It is about what the sinner brings in, not about gold that is already there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון, כפורת and כרובים are permanent parts of the room. The כהן גדול does not carry them in on יום כיפור. The concern is a person coming to ask forgiveness while bringing in a reminder of his sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner (here, the one seeking atonement)
Should not bring near / bring in
This is what we are saying (limits the rule)

phrases.english: What we are saying is: a sinner should not bring in (gold).
phrases.notes: Gold that is already there is not something the sinner brings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ארון.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed no gold at all may be in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only bars the sinner from bringing gold in. Permanent gold fixtures are fine.

steps.title: But the spoon and coal pan are gold and are brought in
steps.stepSummary: The narrowed rule is challenged. On יום כיפור the כהן גדול carries a gold כף and מחתה into the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the spoon and the coal pan, which are gold and are brought in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new version of the rule. The כהן גדול does bring gold items in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the קטורת service on יום כיפור, the כהן גדול carries in a כף of incense and a מחתה of coals, and both are gold. That is exactly a sinner bringing gold in. So the narrowed rule still seems contradicted.

phrases.english: But there is the spoon and the coal pan!
phrases.notes: Both are gold and are carried into the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrowed rule from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a sinner should not bring gold in
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן גדול actually carries the gold כף and מחתה in, so bringing gold in does happen.

steps.title: The rule is only about wearing gold as an ornament
steps.stepSummary: The rule is narrowed again. A sinner should not adorn himself with gold. Tools carried for the service are not ornaments.
steps.simpleTranslation: What we are saying is that a sinner should not beautify himself with gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the rule more exact. It is about wearing gold to look beautiful, not about carrying gold tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כף and מחתה are work tools for the קטורת, not decorations on the person. Dressing up in gold while asking forgiveness for the gold calf is what is improper. That is why the כהן גדול wears white linen inside.

phrases.english: What we are saying is: a sinner should not adorn himself (with gold).
phrases.notes: Tools are not adornment. Clothing is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the כף and מחתה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any gold the sinner brings in is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only gold worn as an ornament is forbidden. Service tools are fine.

steps.title: But he wears gold clothes outside
steps.stepSummary: The rule is challenged again. All year, and even on יום כיפור, the כהן גדול wears gold garments in the outer service.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the gold garments worn outside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'no gold ornaments' rule. The כהן גדול does wear his gold clothes when he serves outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wearing gold recalls the sin, the כהן גדול should never wear his בגדי זהב. Yet he wears them for the outer services, even on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: But there are the golden garments, worn outside!
phrases.notes: The כהן גדול wears these for the service outside the Holy of Holies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'no adornment' rule from Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a sinner may not adorn himself with gold
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן גדול does wear gold clothing during the outer service.

steps.title: The rule applies only inside
steps.stepSummary: The rule only applies inside the קודש הקדשים. Outside, gold clothing is not a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the rule to one place, the קודש הקדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside is where the atonement happens most directly before ה׳. That is where a reminder of the sin would hurt. Outside, the concern does not apply.

phrases.english: We are speaking about inside.
phrases.notes: The rule is limited to the Holy of Holies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the outer gold garments.
steps.terutzMaskana: Gold ornaments are forbidden only inside the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: But the שופר is blown outside too
steps.stepSummary: If the rule only applies inside, it should not apply to a שופר. A שופר is blown outside the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שופר is also outside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the newly narrowed rule back on the original case. If the rule is only for inside, why should a cow's horn שופר be invalid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point was to explain why the רבנן disqualify a cow's horn. Now that the rule is limited to the קודש הקדשים, it seems not to apply to a שופר at all. So the explanation for the רבנן is in danger.

phrases.english: The shofar is also outside!
phrases.notes: It is never blown in the Holy of Holies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the limit from Step 17 to question whether the rule applies to שופר.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's use of רב חסדא's rule to explain the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule only applies inside, and a שופר is blown outside, so the rule cannot disqualify a cow's horn.

steps.title: Shofar is for remembrance, so it counts as inside
steps.stepSummary: The שופר is blown so that ה׳ will remember us favorably. That makes it like a service inside the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is for remembrance, it is considered like inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the 'inside' rule still applies to שופר. The שופר's purpose puts it in the same category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What makes 'inside' special is standing directly before ה׳ to be remembered for good. The שופר does the same thing, so it is treated as if it were inside. A horn that recalls the calf would therefore work against its own purpose.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the 'inside' idea is about function: standing before ה׳. It is not only a physical location.

phrases.english: Since it is for remembrance,
phrases.notes: The shofar brings us to be remembered before God.

phrases.english: it is considered as if inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that a שופר is blown outside.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שופר blown outside falls outside the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the שופר is for remembrance, it is treated as inside, and the rule applies.

steps.title: But the תנא said the reason is that it is a קרן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how can עולא give the 'reminder of the calf' reason? The תנא said a cow's horn is invalid because it is called a קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא said 'because it is a קרן'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's whole explanation. The source text itself gives a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא explicitly says a cow's horn is invalid 'because it is a קרן,' meaning it is called a horn and not a שופר. That is a naming reason, not a reminder-of-sin reason. So עולא's reason seems to clash with the תנא's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who taught the source

phrases.english: But the Tanna
said: 'because it is a keren'!
phrases.notes: Quoting the stated reason for disqualifying a cow's horn.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא קֶרֶן קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that עולא's rule is secured, the גמרא checks it against the תנא's stated reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנא explicitly gives a different reason, 'because it is a קרן,' not 'a prosecutor cannot be a defender.'

steps.title: The תנא gave two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The תנא gave two reasons. First, a prosecutor cannot become a defender. Second, a cow's horn is called a קרן and not a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said one reason and another: one, that a prosecutor cannot become a defender; and another, that it is a קרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons do not conflict. The תנא meant both of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is עולא's: something that recalls the sin cannot plead for us. The second reason is the name: the פסוקים call a cow's horn a קרן. The תנא only stated the second reason openly, but the first reason stands next to it.
steps.whatToRemember: A cow's horn is invalid for two reasons. It recalls the עגל הזהב (a prosecutor cannot become a defender), and it is called a קרן, not a שופר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא dropped the קרן reason. Both reasons are kept side by side.

phrases.english: He stated one reason and another:
one, that a prosecutor cannot become a defender;
phrases.notes: The cow recalls the Golden Calf.

phrases.english: and another, because it is called a keren.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the תנא's stated reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא's 'קרן' reason replaces עולא's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא holds both reasons. עולא's reason is the first, and 'קרן' is the second.

steps.title: How רבי יוסי answers both reasons for invalidating a cow's horn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says אין קטיגור נעשה סניגור applies only inside the קודש הקדשים, and the שופר is blown outside. He also says all שופרות are called קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what would רבי יוסי say? He would tell you: You said a prosecutor cannot become a defender. That is true only inside the קודש הקדשים, and this שופר is blown outside. And you said a cow's horn is invalid because it is called a קרן. But every שופר is also called a קרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי, who allows a cow's horn, would answer the two reasons just given against it. It then gives his answer to each reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer goes back to the simple view from Step 17: the rule against a 'prosecutor' only applies inside the קודש הקדשים. רבי יוסי does not accept the idea from Step 19 that the שופר counts as 'inside.' The second answer takes away the special status of the word קרן, because the Torah uses קרן for every kind of שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: Prosecutor. Here, the cow's horn recalls the sin of the golden calf.
Defender. Something that pleads for us before ה׳.
Inside. This means inside the קודש הקדשים.
Horn. The תנא used this word to argue that a cow's horn is not a שופר.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not denying the rule of אין קטיגור נעשה סניגור. He only limits where the rule applies. In his view the שופר is outside, so the rule does not apply.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei?
phrases.notes: Meaning: how would he answer these arguments?

phrases.english: He would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא אָמְרַתְּ אֵין קָטֵיגוֹר נַעֲשָׂה סָנֵיגוֹר —
phrases.english: That which you said, a prosecutor cannot become a defender —
this applies only inside,
and this shofar is outside.
And that which you said, because it is a keren —
all shofarot are also called keren.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוסי's answer to the two reasons the תנא gave in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of a principle and rejects a proof from wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both reasons seemed to clearly disqualify a cow's horn.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יוסי, neither reason works. The שופר is outside, and every שופר is called a קרן.

steps.title: אביי's reason: a layered horn looks like several שופרות
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the רבנן disqualify a cow's horn because it is made of layers. That makes it look like two or three שופרות, and the Torah requires one שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is the reason of the רבנן. The Torah says 'a שופר,' meaning one, not two or three שופרות. A cow's horn is made of layer upon layer, so it looks like two or three שופרות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a brand-new reason for why the רבנן invalidate a cow's horn. His reason has nothing to do with the golden calf or the word קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'שופר' in the singular, so you may not blow two or three horns joined together. A cow's horn has visible layers, so it looks like several horns stacked together. That is why it is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who offers a new explanation here.
'The Merciful One.' A way of saying the Torah or ה׳.
Layer upon layer, like peels or skins.
It looks like; it appears as.

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the רבנן's ruling based on the physical shape of the horn, not only on the name it is given.

phrases.english: Abaye said,
this is the reason of the Rabbis:
The Merciful One said 'a shofar,'
and not two or three shofarot.
And this horn of a cow,
since it is made of layer upon layer —
it looks like two or three shofarot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new explanation of the רבנן's view, as an alternative to עולא's reason in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cow's horn is invalid because its layers make it look like several שופרות, and the Torah requires one.

steps.title: But the תנא said the reason is that it is a קרן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: the תנא in the משנה clearly gave the reason 'because it is a קרן,' not a reason about layers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא said the reason is 'because it is a קרן'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי. The משנה already gives its own reason, so how can אביי give a different one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא normally does not invent a reason when the משנה states one openly. The משנה says 'because it is a קרן,' which seems to leave no room for אביי's reason about layers.

phrases.english: But the tanna
said 'because it is a keren'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's new reason from Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reason (the layers look like several שופרות)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה openly gives a different reason, so אביי's reason seems to go against the text.

steps.title: The תנא gave two reasons
steps.stepSummary: The תנא meant two reasons: the Torah requires one שופר, not several, and also a cow's horn is called a קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is saying one reason and also another. The first reason: the Torah said one שופר, not two or three. The second reason: it is called a קרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אביי does not go against the משנה. The משנה has two reasons, and אביי is explaining the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase חדא ועוד means 'one reason, and also another.' The תנא only said the second reason out loud, but he also had the reason about layers in mind. This answer follows the same pattern as Step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One, and also another.' A tool for showing that a statement contains two reasons.

steps.confusionAlert: Step 21 also said the תנא had two reasons. There the first reason was אין קטיגור נעשה סניגור. Here the first reason is אביי's point about one שופר. These are two different ways of reading the משנה.

phrases.english: He is saying one reason and also another:
One — that the Merciful One said one shofar,
and not two or three shofarot.
And another — because it is a keren.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the משנה as giving two reasons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to give only one reason: that it is a קרן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה has two reasons, and אביי's reason is the first of them.

steps.title: רבי יוסי rejects אביי's reason too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the layers of a cow's horn are attached to each other, so it counts as one שופר. He also repeats that every שופר is called a קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי would tell you: You said the Torah requires one שופר, not two or three. But since the layers are attached to each other, it is one שופר. And you said it is invalid because it is a קרן. But every שופר is also called a קרן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוסי can also answer אביי's version of the רבנן's two reasons. So רבי יוסי keeps his view that a cow's horn is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of 'one שופר, not two or three' is about separate horns joined together. Layers that grow attached to each other are naturally one horn. רבי יוסי gives the same answer about the word קרן as in Step 22, because the תנא's second reason is the same here.

keyTerms.meaning: They are attached to each other.

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן invalidate a cow's horn for two reasons: (1) either אין קטיגור נעשה סניגור (עולא), or the layers look like several שופרות (אביי); and (2) it is called a קרן. רבי יוסי rejects all of these. The 'prosecutor' rule applies only inside the קודש הקדשים, attached layers count as one horn, and every שופר is called a קרן.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei would say to you:
That which you said, 'The Merciful One said one shofar,
and not two or three shofarot' —
since they are attached to each other,
it is one.
And that which you said, 'because it is a keren' —
all shofarot are also called keren.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends אביי's branch by showing that רבי יוסי can answer it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the comparison: attached layers are one unit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A layered horn looks like several שופרות and should be invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Layers that are attached count as one שופר, so רבי יוסי allows a cow's horn.

steps.title: How do we know the word יובל means a ram?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that the word יובל, which רבי יוסי relied on, means a ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we see that this word 'יובל' is a word for a ram?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבי יוסי's proof in the משנה. It wants to know how we know that 'יובל' means a ram.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי proved that a ram's horn is called a קרן from the פסוק 'במשוך בקרן היובל'. That proof only works if 'יובל' really means a ram. So the גמרא asks for evidence of that meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is it implied? (asking for the source of a meaning)

phrases.english: From where is it implied
that this word 'yovel'
is a term for a ram?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי יוֹבֵלָא לִישָּׁנָא דְּדִכְרָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוסי's proof from 'קרן היובל' and checks that the meaning of יובל is correct.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Evidence that the word יובל means a ram.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא heard Arabians call a ram יובלא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי עקיבא, who heard people in ערביא call a ram 'יובלא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי עקיבא said, 'When I went to ערביא, they called a ram יובלא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. רבי עקיבא heard the word 'יובלא' used for a ram in Arabia.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The language spoken there was related to Hebrew. If people there used 'יובלא' for a ram, we can learn that the Torah's word 'יובל' means a ram too. This supports רבי יוסי's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a method used in the next steps: a rare word in תנ״ך can be explained by how it was used in another place.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Akiva said:
When I went to Arabia,
they called a ram 'yovla.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: כְּשֶׁהָלַכְתִּי לַעֲרַבְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In Arabia a ram was called 'יובלא', so יובל means a ram.

steps.title: In גליא a נדה was called גלמודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא heard people in גליא call a נדה 'גלמודה'. The word means she is separated from her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא said: When I went to גליא, they called a נדה 'גלמודה.' What does גלמודה mean? 'This one is separated from her husband.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just quoted one of רבי עקיבא's travel reports, it now brings another one. This report explains the word 'גלמודה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read as two words: 'גמולה דא', meaning 'this one is separated'. A נדה is separated from her husband, so 'גלמודה' carries the idea of being alone or cut off. That helps explain the word where it appears in תנ״ך.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is a נדה and separated from her husband
Lonely or cut off; the word being explained

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva said:
When I went to Galia,
they called a menstruating woman 'galmudah.'
What does 'galmudah' mean?
This one is separated from her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another travel report from רבי עקיבא, connected to the one in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word גלמודה means a woman separated from her husband, like a נדה.

steps.title: In Africa a מעה coin was called קשיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא heard people in אפריקי call a מעה coin 'קשיטה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא said: When I went to Africa, they called a מעה coin 'קשיטה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third report from רבי עקיבא. In Africa, a small coin called a מעה was called 'קשיטה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us what 'קשיטה' means. It is the name of a coin. The גמרא will next ask why this matters.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva said:
When I went to Africa,
they called a ma'ah coin 'kesitah.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another travel report in the same chain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קשיטה is the name of a מעה coin.

steps.title: Why does it matter that קשיטה is a coin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference this word information makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does this make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need to know that 'קשיטה' means a coin. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants each piece of word information to explain something real. So it asks where the word 'קשיטה' is used.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference of this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the report in step 30 matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the meaning of קשיטה is needed.

steps.title: It explains the hundred קשיטה in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The Torah says יעקב bought land for 'מאה קשיטה'. This means one hundred coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: To explain 'a hundred קשיטה' in the Torah: it means a hundred coins (דנקי).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The word explains the פסוק where יעקב buys a field near שכם for 'מאה קשיטה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this report, we would not know what 'קשיטה' means in the פסוק. Now we know it was a coin, so יעקב paid one hundred small coins.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the Torah (written in the Torah)

phrases.english: To explain 'a hundred kesitah' in the Torah,
as one hundred coins (dankei).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It explains the Torah's 'מאה קשיטה' as one hundred coins.

steps.title: In the sea towns a sale was called כירה
steps.stepSummary: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) heard people in the coastal cities call a sale 'כירה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: When I went to the sea towns, they called a sale 'כירה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a similar report, this time from רבי. In the coastal towns, the word 'כירה' meant a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method is the same as רבי עקיבא's. This report teaches that the root כ-ר-ה can mean buying or selling.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה
כירה, the local word for a sale

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
When I went to the sea towns,
they called a sale 'kirah.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of word reports with a new speaker.

steps.title: Why does it matter that כירה means a sale?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks what practical difference this makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does this make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question as before, now about 'כירה'. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats: the גמרא wants to know which פסוק this meaning helps explain.

phrases.english: What is the practical difference of this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the report in step 33 matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק the meaning of כירה explains.

steps.title: It explains יעקב's words: the grave I bought
steps.stepSummary: The word explains יעקב's words 'אשר כריתי לי': the grave that I bought for myself.
steps.simpleTranslation: To explain 'which I כריתי for myself': meaning 'which I bought for myself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers. The word 'כריתי' in יעקב's request about his burial place means 'I bought'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think 'כריתי' means 'I dug'. The report from the sea towns shows it can mean 'I bought'. So יעקב was talking about a grave he purchased.

keyTerms.meaning: Which I bought (or dug) for myself (בראשית נ:ה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'כריתי' only means 'I dug'. This גמרא teaches that it can also mean 'I bought'.

phrases.english: To explain 'which I kariti for myself' (which I bought for myself).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It explains 'אשר כריתי לי' as 'which I bought for myself'.

steps.title: In קן נשרייא a bride was נינפי and a rooster שכוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש heard a bride called 'נינפי' and a rooster called 'שכוי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: When I went to the district of קן נשרייא, they called a bride 'נינפי' and a rooster 'שכוי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more travel report, from רבי שמעון בן לקיש. It gives two words: 'נינפי' for a bride and 'שכוי' for a rooster.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two words will each be connected to a פסוק in the next steps. The method is the same as before.

keyTerms.meaning: נינפי, the local word for a bride
שכוי, the local word for a rooster

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
When I went to the district of Kan Nishrayya,
they called a bride 'ninfi,'
and a rooster 'sekhvi.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: כְּשֶׁהָלַכְתִּי לִתְחוּם קַן נִשְׁרַיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of word reports with a new speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נינפי means a bride, and שכוי means a rooster.

steps.title: The verse for נינפי: beautiful view, joy of the earth
steps.stepSummary: The word נינפי explains 'יפה נוף' in תהלים. Mount Zion is beautiful like a bride.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bride is called 'נינפי.' What is the verse? 'Beautiful נוף, the joy of the whole earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which פסוק the word 'נינפי' explains. It is 'יפה נוף משוש כל הארץ' (תהלים מח:ג).
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'נוף' sounds like 'נינפי'. So 'יפה נוף' means 'beautiful like a bride'. The פסוק is praising הר ציון as being as beautiful as a bride.

keyTerms.meaning: Beautiful in view; here: beautiful like a bride

phrases.english: A bride is called 'ninfi':
what is the verse?
'Beautiful nof, the joy of the whole earth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the first word from step 36 to a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נינפי explains 'יפה נוף' as beautiful like a bride.

steps.title: The verse for שכוי: who gave understanding to the שכוי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב (or, some say, רבי יהושע בן לוי) says the word שכוי explains a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a rooster is called 'שכוי.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב, or if you wish, say it was רבי יהושע בן לוי: What is the verse? 'Who has put wisdom in the inward parts, or who has given understanding to the שכוי?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which פסוק the word 'שכוי' explains. It is איוב לח:לו. The גמרא is unsure who said this teaching, so it gives two possible names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'שכוי' means a rooster, the פסוק is talking about the understanding given to a rooster. The phrase 'ואיבעית אימא' only tells us there is doubt about who said it. It does not change the teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (here: an alternate attribution)
The hidden inner parts of the body

phrases.english: And a rooster is called 'sekhvi':
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: and if you wish, say it was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
What is the verse?
'Who has put wisdom in the inward parts,
or who has given understanding to the sekhvi?'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַתַּרְנְגוֹל שֶׂכְוִי — אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the second word from step 36 to a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שכוי in איוב לח:לו means a rooster.

steps.title: Explaining the verse: the kidneys and the rooster
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is explained part by part: 'טחות' are the kidneys, and 'שכוי' is the rooster.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who has put wisdom in the inward parts': these are the kidneys. 'Or who has given understanding to the שכוי': this is the rooster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each half of the פסוק from איוב. This finishes רבי שמעון בן לקיש's report, but the series of word stories continues in the next step with a story about לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hidden 'inward parts' are the kidneys, which were thought to give a person wise advice. The 'שכוי' is the rooster, which ה׳ gave the understanding to know when to crow at night. So the meaning 'rooster' fits the פסוק well.
steps.whatToRemember: The word יובל means a ram, as רבי עקיבא heard in ערביא. This supports רבי יוסי's proof that a ram's horn is called a קרן. The גמרא then lists other rare words in תנ״ך that are explained by how people spoke in other places: גלמודה, קשיטה, כירה, נוף, and שכוי.

phrases.english: 'Who has put wisdom in the inward parts':
these are the kidneys;
'or who has given understanding to the sekhvi':
this is the rooster.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 38 and completes רבי שמעון בן לקיש's report; the series continues with the story about לוי in step 40.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שכוי in איוב means a rooster, and טחות are the kidneys. This completes רבי שמעון בן לקיש's report; the series of word stories continues with לוי.

steps.title: Levi arrives in a certain place and a man approaches him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: לוי came to a certain place, a man came before him and spoke to him. This sets up a strange word the man is about to say.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי happened to come to a certain place. A man came before him and said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new story about לוי. This line is only the setup; the important words the man says come in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have been seeing how the חכמים learned the meaning of hard words by hearing how people speak in other places. This story follows the same pattern: לוי is in an unfamiliar place, and a local man is about to use a word that will matter. Nothing is ruled or proven yet; the scene is just being set.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא, a student of רבי יהודה הנשיא. He is the main character of this story.
Happened to come to, arrived at (often while traveling)
Before him, in front of him (here: coming to him with a complaint or a case)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a ruling or a question here. This line only sets the scene. The point of the story, a local word, comes right after 'אמר ליה'.

phrases.english: Levi happened to come to a certain place.
phrases.notes: Typical opening for a travel story in the גמרא.

phrases.english: A man came before him,
phrases.notes: Coming 'before' a חכם usually means bringing a complaint or a case for judgment.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Opens the man's words, which continue on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of stories about learning word meanings from how people speak in other places, after the explanations of נינפי and שכוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This is a narrative opening that sets up a local man's statement containing a word whose meaning will be clarified.
